questions.question: A job writes thousands of log lines per minute and you need to watch one value while it runs. What capability do you need?
options: Reopen the whole file by hand every second and scan it visually
Print the entire file from the start on every check
Wait until the job ends, then read everything
Stream the growing file and filter it for that value
questions.explanation: A growing log needs a streaming filter, not repeated full reads. This lesson builds that habit into reusable shell helpers for following training output.

questions.question: What is the difference between these redirections: > output.log and >> output.log?
options: > appends; >> truncates the file before writing
Both send output to the terminal and leave the file unchanged
Both redirect only standard error
> replaces; >> appends
questions.explanation: A single greater-than opens the destination for replacement, while the double form opens it for append. Use the latter when preserving earlier training runs matters.

questions.question: Why is tmux useful for a long training run on an SSH GPU box?
options: Detach and reattach to the same session
It turns a failed training process into a system service automatically
It doubles the GPU VRAM available to Python
It compresses every checkpoint before the program writes it
questions.explanation: The tmux server stays alive after the SSH client disconnects. Reattaching shows the same shell and output, and panes can hold training and monitoring commands together.

questions.question: Which command copies a local experiment directory to a remote GPU box while preserving useful file metadata?
options: grep -r experiment user@gpu-box
rsync -av over SSH
nvidia-smi ./experiment/ user@gpu-box
python -m scp --metadata ./experiment/
questions.explanation: rsync's archive mode preserves common metadata and transfers the directory over SSH. It can later send only changed files.

questions.question: You lose your SSH connection halfway through training and want to see whether the job continues. What should you do next time?
options: Run it in the foreground and close the terminal quickly
Pipe stderr to /dev/null so SIGHUP cannot reach the process
Run it inside tmux
Copy the command into the local browser address bar
questions.explanation: A tmux session owns the shell independently of the SSH client. After reconnecting, tmux attach restores the running view instead of relying on a fragile foreground process.

questions.question: Which sequence gives a useful remote training workspace with live GPU monitoring?
options: Start nvidia-smi on the laptop, then copy its screen into the remote shell
Use scp to execute the training loop and delete the remote log
Run the job with > /dev/null so no process needs monitoring
Use tmux with a monitoring pane
questions.explanation: The session keeps the job alive, a second pane exposes device utilization, and reattachment preserves both views. Logging stdout and stderr separately can complement the live pane.
